sections.param_extraction: The stage that fits parametric z profiles to focused cubes, producing the per-pixel Gaussian-mixture ground truth the backbone learns to predict. It runs constrained optimization over each preprocessed cube and recomputes fit metrics and diagnostic plots for existing trials. The configs here control optimizer iteration caps and fit hyperparameters, the single-run extraction driver, the batch entry point that sweeps datasets and hyperparameter grids, and the inference config that regenerates metrics and summaries.
sections.normalization: The stage that standardizes network inputs and outputs, mapping heavy-tailed input channels and Gaussian parameters onto stable numeric ranges for training and inference. It fits per-channel location/scale transforms from pixel statistics, persists them, and bounds predicted outputs to a physically valid range. The configs here control per-channel normalization recipes, per-slot strategy selection for input and output channels, runtime output clamping, and the persisted fitted statistics applied at train and inference time.
sections.dataset: The stage that assembles trainable examples from a preprocessed dataset run. It selects input and target channels, tiles cropped scenes into overlapping patches, applies augmentation, and builds the train/val/test dataloaders. The configs here control which stack channels and Aux form the input, which per-Gaussian parameters are predicted, patch tiling and augmentation, and the parallel assembly of the image-patch datasets.
sections.architectures: The stage that defines the backbone architectures. Each config specifies one model variant's layer geometry, output-head structure, and per-group optimizer settings. The configs here cover U-Net and transformer backbones predicting per-pixel Gaussian-mixture parameters.
sections.training: The stage that optimizes the backbone. It binds architecture, loss, optimization, scheduling, and runtime sub-configs into one resolved run and manages queuing and sweeps. The configs here control loss term weighting, optimizer, scheduler, warmup, early-stopping and gradient-clipping policy, filesystem layout, VRAM reservation and resource monitoring, and the trainer and entry configs.
sections.resources: Host and device sampling settings shared by every training family: whether the resource monitor runs, how often it samples CPU, RAM, shared memory and GPU memory, whether samples go to TensorBoard, and the utilisation levels that raise a warning in the run log. They live outside the training package so that a long-running processing entry can carry them without importing torch.
sections.inference: The stage that runs trained checkpoints over data splits to produce predictions, evaluations, and reports. It drives sliding-window prediction for backbone runs, scheduling one worker per run across a GPU pool. The configs here control the per-run inference driver, its output subdirectory and filename layout, and the batch entry point that queues inference across all discovered runs.
sections.benchmark: The stage that compares multiple model architectures on the same data. It trains each backbone at its own configured size, runs inference, and assembles a cross-model comparison report. The configs here control batched inference and its diagnostic artifacts, the comparison report assembly, and the top-level sweep orchestration.
sections.cross_validation: The stage that estimates generalization by partitioning the stack along row into k folds and training and evaluating on each. It orchestrates per-fold training, inference, and comparison for the backbone. The configs here control the row-range fold partitioning and the top-level k-fold orchestration.
sections.tuning: The stage that searches hyperparameter spaces with Optuna to improve a chosen backbone. It wires the search budget, pruning, and resources to a nested training configuration and swaps in per-trial hyperparameter samples. The configs here control the Optuna search controls and artifact emission, and the entry point binding resources and data to the search.
sections.comparison: The stage that rebuilds side-by-side comparisons across completed runs and trials without re-running training or inference. It aggregates existing inference or preprocessing outputs into a single report grouped by the varied factor. The configs here control comparison of backbone inference runs, of preprocessing trials differing by multilook window, of Gaussian-fit extraction trials grouped by component count, and the standalone rebuild of an existing benchmark comparison report.
sections.diagnostics: The stage that inspects completed training runs independently of any data run. The weight-xray diagnostic classifies each checkpoint tensor against numeric thresholds and emits a per-run report and plots; the tensorboard export renders every logged scalar series as a publication-quality figure inside the run directory, pairing train and validation series of the same metric in one shared figure. The configs here control the pathology classification thresholds, the single-run diagnostics and their report and plot outputs, and the batch webui entries that select runs and build a per-run configuration.
sections.synthesis: The stage that generates the bundled example dataset, so the template runs end to end without external data. It draws smooth per-pixel Gaussian-mixture parameter fields, renders them into z profiles, derives a multi-channel input stack with a matching Aux, and writes the dataset, its parameter run and the metadata the downstream stages expect. The configs here control the scene extent and z axis, the mixture statistics, the channel synthesis and noise levels, the fit metadata written alongside the parameters, and the entry point that runs the generator.

param_extraction::FitConfig.summary: Gaussian-fit hyperparameters and per-parameter free/frozen toggles for one profile-fitting run

fields.threshold_factor: profile preprocessing floor: samples below this fraction of the per-pixel profile maximum are zeroed before fitting
fields.truncation_index: profile preprocessing cut: z-axis samples at or above this index are zeroed before fitting
fields.k_max: maximum number of Gaussian components; every K from 1 to k_max is fitted and the penalised best is kept
fields.lambda_k: component-count regularization strength added as lambda_k * K to each K's MSE for best-K selection
fields.prominence_frac: peak prominence threshold for the CPU initialiser as a fraction of the per-pixel profile maximum
fields.sigma_init_divisor: divisor shrinking the z-span-derived base width (h_span/(8*k_max), floored at 2 bin spacings) into each Gaussian's initial sigma guess
fields.activity_threshold: per-pixel profile maximum at or below which the pixel is skipped by the fit and keeps zero parameters; recorded in param_extraction_meta.json as the activity_threshold every training, inference and analysis stage reads for this parameter run
fields.fit_sigma: toggle freeing the Gaussian widths during the Adam fit; off masks their gradients so they stay at the initial guess
fields.fit_amplitude: toggle freeing the Gaussian amplitudes during the Adam fit; off masks their gradients so they stay at the initial guess
fields.fit_mean: toggle freeing the Gaussian mean z values during the Adam fit; off masks their gradients so they stay at the initial guess

param_extraction::FitSettings.summary: Gaussian-fit hyperparameters for one profile-fitting run

fields.fit_config: FitConfig sub-config with k_max, lambda_k, sigma_init_divisor, thresholds, and the fit_sigma/fit_amplitude/fit_mean free-parameter toggles

param_extraction::ExtractionConfig.summary: Drives one Gaussian-mixture parameter-extraction run over a single preprocessed cube

fields.processed_data_path: root of the preprocessed run holding data/ and meta/ subfolders, source of the cube to fit
fields.output_prefix: leading token of the generated output subdirectory name, joined with the hyperparameter suffix
fields.output_suffix: optional fixed naming tag overriding the auto-derived k/lambda/sigma/free-params suffix
fields.z_range: reconstruction z-axis extent as (min, max); None reads it from meta/config_state.json
fields.fit_settings: FitSettings sub-config bundling the iteration cap and Gaussian-fit hyperparameters (k_max, lambda_k, sigma_init_divisor, free-parameter flags)
fields.parameter_workers: number of CPU worker processes in the PeakInitialiser pool used for per-pixel peak-based initial guesses
fields.col_batch_size: number of range bins loaded and fit together per batch while streaming the cube
fields.gpu_pixel_batch_size: fixed number of pixels per GPU batch the JAX Adam-fit kernel is compiled and iterated over, with padding to keep every batch this size
fields.adam_steps: number of Adam optimizer steps run per pixel batch during Gaussian curve fitting
fields.adam_lr: Adam learning rate for the per-pixel Gaussian curve-fitting optimizer
fields.adam_b1: Adam beta1 first-moment decay coefficient for the Gaussian curve-fitting optimizer
fields.adam_b2: Adam beta2 second-moment decay coefficient for the Gaussian curve-fitting optimizer

fields.fit_lambda_values: list of component-count regularization strengths (lambda_k) to sweep, one extraction plan per value

fields.adam_steps: number of Adam optimizer steps run per pixel batch during Gaussian curve fitting, shared across the sweep
fields.adam_lr: Adam learning rate for the per-pixel Gaussian curve-fitting optimizer, shared across the sweep
fields.gpu_device_ids: GPU indices pinned via EnvironmentPinner.gpus before extraction runs
fields.col_batch_size: number of range bins loaded and fit together per batch, shared across the sweep
fields.gpu_pixel_batch_size: fixed number of pixels per GPU batch the JAX Adam-fit kernel is compiled and iterated over, shared across the sweep

normalization/general::ChannelStrategy.summary: Per-channel normalization recipe: fits a location/scale pair from pixel statistics, or returns a fixed constant for fixed_div_pi

fields.norm_method: Statistic used to fit offset/scale: min_max_p999, robust_iqr, or zscore fitted from data; fixed_div_pi is a data-free constant
fields.apply_log1p: Whether to log1p-compress non-negative values before fitting and before applying the location-scale statistics, default False

normalization/general::OutputClampConfig.summary: Runtime clamp bundle bounding predicted Gaussian outputs to a valid physical range

fields.enabled: Gates only the floor/ceil clamp applied when decompressing log1p output channels (out/amp, out/sigma by default); the amp/mu/sigma physical-range clamp in GaussianClamp always applies regardless, default True
fields.floor: Lower bound of the physical value used when decompressing log1p-transformed output channels (out/amp, out/sigma by default), active only when enabled is True, default 0.0
fields.ceil: Upper bound of the physical value used when decompressing log1p-transformed output channels (out/amp, out/sigma by default), active only when enabled is True, default 200.0
fields.leaky_slope: Leak slope of the normalization decompress/compress clamps in the loss path so gradients survive saturation, default 0.1
fields.param_leaky_slope: Leak slope of the GaussianClamp physical parameter-bounds clamp, kept separate from leaky_slope so the stacked below-floor gradient (leaky_slope squared times param_leaky_slope) stays controllable, default 0.1
fields.amp_max: Physical amplitude ceiling applied by GaussianClamp in the loss path and at inference, default 200.0

normalization/general::NormalizationConf.summary: Selects per-slot normalization strategies for input/output channels and output clamping

fields.input_strategy: Global input preset name applied to every input channel group, or per_slot for the built-in slot-specific defaults
fields.output_strategy: Global output preset name applied to every output channel, or per_slot for the built-in slot-specific defaults
fields.chan_mag: Override preset for the per-channel magnitude slot; default keeps the input_strategy/per_slot choice
fields.channel_phase: Override preset for the per-channel phase slot; default keeps the input_strategy/per_slot choice
fields.derived_mag: Override preset for the derived magnitude channel; default keeps the input_strategy/per_slot choice
fields.derived_phase: Override preset for the derived phase channel; default keeps the input_strategy/per_slot choice
fields.out_amp: Override preset for the output Gaussian amplitude channel; default keeps the output_strategy/per_slot choice
fields.out_mu: Override preset for the output Gaussian mean/z channel; default keeps the output_strategy/per_slot choice
fields.out_sigma: Override preset for the output Gaussian width channel; default keeps the output_strategy/per_slot choice
fields.aux: Override preset for the Aux z channel; default keeps the input_strategy/per_slot choice
fields.clamp_output: Gates the whole output clamping stack: the clamp_floor/clamp_ceil bound on log1p decompression, the barrier clamp on non-log clampable channels, and the GaussianClamp amp/mu/sigma physical-range clamp in both the training loss and the inference wrapper; False leaves predictions fully unconstrained, default True
fields.clamp_floor: Lower bound of the physical value used when decompressing log1p-transformed output channels (out/amp, out/sigma by default), active only when clamp_output is True, default 0.0
fields.clamp_ceil: Upper bound of the physical value used when decompressing log1p-transformed output channels (out/amp, out/sigma by default), active only when clamp_output is True, default 200.0
fields.clamp_leaky_slope: Leak slope of the normalization decompress/compress clamps in the loss path (denormalize floor/ceil, renormalize floor) so gradients survive saturation; inference always hard-clamps; default 0.1
fields.param_clamp_leaky_slope: Leak slope of the Gaussian physical parameter-bounds clamp in the loss path, separate from clamp_leaky_slope so the stacked below-floor gradient (clamp_leaky_slope squared times param_clamp_leaky_slope) stays controllable, default 0.1
fields.amp_max: Physical amplitude ceiling of the Gaussian parameter clamp, applied in the loss and at inference, default 200.0

normalization/general::ChannelStats.summary: Persisted fitted normalization statistics per channel for applying transforms at train/inference time

fields.loc: Per-channel offset subtracted during normalization: a low percentile, the median, the mean, or 0.0, depending on the fitted norm_method
fields.scale: Per-channel divisor (std, IQR, range, or pi) applied during normalization
fields.names: Optional per-channel slot labels aligned with loc/scale entries
fields.strategies: Optional per-channel ChannelStrategy recording the fitting method (norm_method, apply_log1p) used
fields.clampable: Per-channel flag marking physical values bounded by the output clamp on denormalization; true for out/amp and out/sigma, false for out/mu and all input channels

dataset/gaussian::GaussianConfig.summary: Gaussian-mixture head geometry: component count and z-axis bounds for the cube profile

fields.n_default_gaussians: Number of Gaussian components (K) predicted per pixel, derived from param_extraction_meta.json k_max and propagated to dataset_config.n_gaussians and out_channels
fields.x_min: Lower bound of the z axis, taken from the dataset's cube_config.z_range and used to build the GaussianAxis for curve synthesis
fields.x_max: Upper bound of the z axis, taken from the dataset's cube_config.z_range and used to build the GaussianAxis for curve synthesis
fields.activity_threshold: Physical amplitude above which a Gaussian slot counts as active (a strict comparison shared by every stage through GaussianActivity.is_active), read from param_extraction_meta.json activity_threshold of the label run; it is chosen once at extraction or synthesis and every training, inference and analysis stage reads it from here instead of asking again
fields.params_per_gaussian: Number of predicted parameters per Gaussian component (amplitude, mean, sigma = 3); out_channels must be an exact multiple of it

dataset/general/dataset::InputConfig.summary: Selects which stack channels and Aux feed the network input and their per-channel channel encoding

fields.use_primary: include the primary reference channel in the input stack
fields.primary_representation: channel encoding of the primary channel: real_imag, mag_real_imag, mag_angle, mag_ri_angle, angle_only, or mag_only
fields.use_secondaries: include secondary channels, requires the dataset stack to actually contain secondaries or the dataset build raises
fields.secondaries_representation: channel encoding applied to each secondary channel: real_imag, mag_real_imag, mag_angle, mag_ri_angle, angle_only, or mag_only
fields.use_derived: include primary-secondary derived channels, requires the dataset stack to contain derived or the dataset build raises
fields.derived_representation: channel encoding applied to each derived: real_imag, mag_real_imag, mag_angle, mag_ri_angle, angle_only, or mag_only
fields.use_aux: append a single Aux z channel to the input, requires the cropper to supply a Aux array or the dataset build raises

dataset/general/dataset::OutputConfig.summary: Fixed per-Gaussian parameter layout the backbone predicts and the normalization strategy of each role

fields.ROLE_NAMES: Class-level fixed per-Gaussian parameter layout a, mu, sig, matching the three channels the Gaussian head emits and the ground-truth stack stores
fields.output_strategies: per-role ChannelStrategy (norm method plus optional log1p) for the out/amp, out/mu, out/sigma channels, defaults to per-slot presets and rebuilt from NormalizationConfig by the config factory

dataset/general/dataset::PatchConfig.summary: Tiling of cropped scenes into overlapping training/inference patches

fields.size: patch z and width in pixels as a (H, W) tuple; the two dimensions may differ for rectangular patches
fields.stride: pixel step between adjacent patch origins as a per-axis (vertical, horizontal) tuple, entries smaller than the matching size give overlapping patches
fields.use_symmetric_padding: pad scene borders with numpy symmetric (mirror, edge-duplicating) padding instead of zero (constant) padding so edge patches are still fully covered

dataset/general/dataset::AugmentationCon.summary: Random spatial and noise augmentation probabilities applied to training patches

fields.p_flip_h: probability of a horizontal (left-right) flip applied to a training patch
fields.p_flip_v: probability of a vertical (up-down) flip applied to a training patch
fields.p_rot90: probability of a random 90-degree rotation applied to a training patch, default disabled
fields.noise_std: standard deviation of additive Gaussian noise injected into patch channels when p_noise triggers
fields.p_noise: probability of adding Gaussian noise (noise_std) to a training patch, default disabled

dataset/general/dataset::DatasetConfig.summary: Assembles the patch dataset and dataloaders from a preprocessed dataset run for backbone training and inference

fields.preprocessing_run_directory: path to the preprocessed run directory whose stack, parameters, and metadata the Layout loads from
fields.fingerprint_dataset: whether the training run hashes the dataset artifacts into meta/dataset_fingerprint.json for provenance; propagated from paths.fingerprint_dataset by the config factory
fields.split_regions: SplitRegions of train/val/test CropRegion(s) partitioning the scene spatially before patching
fields.parameters_path: optional override path to the run's extracted acquisition parameters file, left None it is never auto-derived from preprocessing_run_directory and Layout will fail to resolve it
fields.secondary_labels: ordered tuple of secondary-channel identifiers to select from the stack, None keeps all available channels
fields.patch: PatchConfig sub-config for patch size, stride, and border-padding mode
fields.input_config: InputConfig sub-config selecting which channel groups (primary, secondaries, derived, Aux) and encodings feed the network
fields.output_config: OutputConfig sub-config selecting which Gaussian parameters (amplitude, mu, sigma) are predicted and their normalization strategies
fields.normalization: NormalizationConfig sub-config selecting per-slot channel normalization strategies (percentile, robust-IQR, zscore, fixed-div-pi, optional log1p) for chan/derived/Aux/output channels plus the output clamp floor, ceil, and leaky slopes
fields.augmentation: AugmentationConfig sub-config setting horizontal/vertical flip, rot90, and additive-noise probabilities applied to training patches
fields.batch_size: number of patches per optimization step in the dataloader
fields.num_workers: number of dataloader worker processes used for parallel patch loading
fields.prefetch_factor: number of batches each dataloader worker prefetches ahead of consumption
fields.shuffle_train: shuffle patch order every epoch for the training split only
fields.pin_memory: pin host memory in the dataloader for faster host-to-GPU transfer
fields.z_axis: z sampling grid for the Gaussian mixture, populated at launch via GaussianAxis.build from the gaussian config's x_min/x_max and profile length

architectures/backbone::UNetConfig.summary: Plain U-Net backbone predicting per-pixel Gaussian mixture parameters over the z profile

fields.in_channels: Number of input feature-map channels fed to the network, overridden at build time by the dataset's assembled channel count (primary + secondaries + derived + Aux)
fields.out_channels: Number of output channels, equal to n_gaussians x params_per_gaussian and required to be divisible by params_per_gaussian
fields.params_per_gaussian: Number of predicted parameters per Gaussian component (amplitude, mean, sigma = 3); out_channels must be an exact multiple of it
fields.head: Output head attached to the backbone embedding: conv (single conv projection), multihead (3 PixelMLP heads, one per parameter type), per_gaussian (K PixelMLP heads, one per slot), or set_pred (per-slot heads plus a sigmoid existence gate)
fields.features: Per-level encoder channel widths, one entry per resolution stage, ascending order by convention; default [64, 128, 256, 512]
fields.bottleneck_factor: Channel-width multiplier for the U-Net bottleneck relative to the deepest encoder level; categorical over {1, 2, 4}
fields.dropout: Dropout probability applied in conv/MLP/attention blocks, 0.0 disables it; tuned over roughly 0.0-0.5
fields.activation: Nonlinearity used in conv blocks: relu, leaky_relu, gelu, silu, or elu; hyperparameter tuning samples only the first four
fields.normalization: Convolutional normalization layer applied inside blocks: batch, instance, group, or none (identity); tuning samples only the first three
fields.upsample_mode: Decoder upsampling operator: convtranspose (learned) or bilinear (fixed interpolation)
fields.conv_bias: Whether convolution layers carry an additive bias term, usually disabled when a normalization layer follows
fields.init_mode: Weight initialization scheme for conv/linear layers: default (framework default, no override), kaiming, or xavier
fields.encoder_lr: Learning rate for the encoder parameter group, tuned log-uniform over 1e-5..1e-2
fields.bottleneck_lr: Learning rate for the bottleneck parameter group, tuned log-uniform over 1e-5..1e-2
fields.decoder_lr: Learning rate for the decoder parameter group, tuned log-uniform over 1e-5..1e-2
fields.output_head_lr: Learning rate for the output-head parameter group that maps decoder features to Gaussian parameters, defaults higher (1e-3) than the backbone groups
fields.encoder_wd: Weight decay for the encoder parameter group, tuned log-uniform over 1e-6..1e-1
fields.bottleneck_wd: Weight decay for the bottleneck parameter group, tuned log-uniform over 1e-6..1e-1
fields.decoder_wd: Weight decay for the decoder parameter group, tuned log-uniform over 1e-6..1e-1
fields.output_head_wd: Weight decay for the output-head parameter group, tuned log-uniform over 1e-6..1e-1
fields.shape_logger_types: Tuple of nn.Module classes (conv, pool, norm, activation) whose per-layer output shapes are captured by the forward-hook model-documentation trace run once per training run on a real batch

fields.leaky_slopes: Leak slopes kept outside the clamp bounds for curve outputs, one leaky rung each; all must be positive and unique so every rung differs from the hard clamp
fields.param_leaky_slopes: Leak slopes kept outside the clamp bounds for Gaussian parameter outputs, paired with leaky_slopes by position; must match its length and stay positive

training/backbone::EmaTrialsConfig.summary: Weight-EMA ladder for the ema trial planner: rung 0 trains and checkpoints the raw weights, then one rung per configured decay tracks an exponential moving average of the weights at that decay

fields.decays: EMA decay rates, one raw rung and one decay-warmup rung each; all must lie strictly between 0 and 1 and be unique

training/backbone::StabilityTrialsConfig.summary: Cumulative training-stability ladder for the stability trial planner: rung 0 trains without lr warmup and without gradient clipping, then one warmup rung per configured fraction of the total optimizer steps, then one clipping rung per configured norm threshold on top of the first warmup

fields.warmup_fractions: Fractions of the run's total optimizer steps the learning-rate warmup ramp spans, one warmup-only rung each; all must lie in (0, 1] and be unique, and the first also underlies the combined warmup-plus-clipping rungs
fields.warmup_mode: Shape of the warmup ramp on those rungs, one of linear, cosine, exponential or polynomial
fields.clip_mode: Gradient-clipping strategy of the clipping rungs, one of fixed, adaptive_percentile or adaptive_mean_std; disabled is rejected because it would repeat the warmup rungs
fields.max_grad_norms: Gradient-norm thresholds of the fixed clipping strategy, one clipping-only rung and one combined rung each; all must be positive and unique, and only the fixed strategy may list more than one

training/backbone::PatchTrialsConfig.summary: Rectangular patch-shape grid swept by the patch trials mode under a constant pixel budget

fields.minimum: Smallest (rows, cols) patch shape included in pixels; 0 on an axis starts that axis at one admissible step
fields.maximum: Largest (rows, cols) patch shape included in pixels; each axis runs from its start to this bound in steps of the admissible step
fields.step: Spacing between consecutive patch lengths in pixels, shared by both axes; 0 derives it from the backbone's encoder pyramid as 2^levels so every length stays divisible through all downsampling stages (verified one-halving-per-stage U-Nets only, others must set it explicitly)
fields.stride_ratio: Patch stride as a fraction of the patch length per axis, valid range (0, 1]; 0.5 gives 50% overlap
fields.constant_pixel_budget: When true, each trial's batch size and lr_reference_batch_size are rescaled together so batch x row x range matches the reference training.batch_size x training.patch_size pixels, keeping pixels per step and the batch-linear LR scale identical across patch shapes; the max-batch probe is disabled for every patch trial either way so the comparison stays controlled

training/backbone::ReachTrialsConfig.summary: Size-matched architecture comparison at a fixed spatial reach: every rung trains on the same patch with the same parameter budget, so the only free variable left is the architecture

fields.rungs: Architectures compared one run each, every rung a dict of label, backbone and optional model-config overrides; defaults pair an eight-block local_cnn (3x3 ConvBlocks give a 4n+1 = 33x33 receptive field, width 479) against a default unet, both about 31.0 M parameters on the 32x32 patch that a 33x33 receptive field fully covers, with dropout and trunk weight decay pinned to the unet regime (0.15 / 1e-4) on both arms so regularization cannot confound the architecture comparison. Every backbone must exist in the backbone registry and the rungs must stay size matched to within match_tolerance
fields.patch_size: Patch size (rows, cols) in pixels shared by every rung, deliberately square and no larger than the local rung's receptive field so all arms reach the whole patch and reach cannot confound the architecture comparison
fields.patch_stride: Patch stride (rows, cols) in pixels shared by every rung; half of patch_size gives 50% overlap
fields.in_channels: Input channel count the planner builds each rung at when it counts parameters; validated loudly against the channels the input configuration and secondary selection actually produce, because training builds every arm at the dataset width and a mismatch would make the capacity check count the wrong first layer
fields.match_tolerance: Largest fractional spread in parameter count tolerated across the rungs; the planner counts every rung at the configured head before launching and refuses the sweep beyond this, because an unmatched arm turns an architecture result into a capacity result

training/backbone::SecondaryTrialsConfig.summary: Controls how secondary-channel combinations are sampled for the secondary-selection trial sweep

fields.strategy: Secondary-channel sampling scheme: uniform, gaussian, consecutive, spaced, or exhaustive (every combination of exactly n_secondaries channels)
fields.n_secondaries: Number of secondary channels the strategy picks per trial on top of the fixed ones (exact set size for the exhaustive strategy), must be between 1 and the swept candidate count
fields.fixed: Channel labels pinned into every trial and removed from the swept pool, so one fixed channel with n_secondaries 1 under the exhaustive strategy pairs that channel with each remaining secondary in turn
fields.n_trials: Number of distinct secondary-channel draws to generate, required (>=1) for uniform and gaussian strategies
fields.mean: Mean index of the gaussian strategy's normal draw over the secondary-channel list; required (not None) when strategy is gaussian
fields.sigma: Standard deviation of the gaussian strategy's normal draw over the secondary-channel list; required (not None) when strategy is gaussian
fields.block_step: Step between successive window start indices, used by the consecutive and spaced strategies, must be >= 1
fields.spacing: Index gap between selected channels within one window, used by the spaced strategy only, must be >= 1
fields.seed: Random seed for the uniform and gaussian sampling draws, making the trial set reproducible

training/backbone::BackboneEntryConfig.summary: Top-level entry config launching one backbone training run or fanning out a multi-trial GPU sweep

fields.resume: Reuse this run directory when it already holds a completed run (complete.json marker stamped only at successful completion), rerunning inference only if it is missing; an unfinished run directory is deleted and restarted from scratch. The configuration the run or sweep recorded (docs/resolved_entry_config.json of a run, batch_train_logs/resolved_config.json of a sweep) is loaded as the base, the overrides typed on this launch are applied on top and the hardware fields follow this launch; complete units are reused, unfinished units continue from their trainer state or restart in their own directory, and missing units are created, each job handed its exact directory so the naming scheme never has to be reproduced. fields.model_overrides: Dict of architecture-config field overrides applied to the selected backbone before instantiation
fields.paths: TrainingPathsConfig sub-config holding filesystem locations for the dataset, extracted parameters, and secondary-channel labels

fields.input: InputConfig sub-config selecting which channel groups (primary, secondaries, derived, Aux) feed the network, defaults to the full stack
fields.normalization: NormalizationConfig sub-config controlling per-channel input/output normalization strategies and output clamping
fields.augmentation: AugmentationConfig sub-config setting horizontal/vertical flip, rot90, and additive-noise probabilities applied to training patches
fields.infer_after: Run the InferencePipeline automatically on the trained checkpoint once training completes
fields.infer_at_end: Hold all inference until every training job of the fan-out has finished, then run one inference job per completed run through the same GPU queue; keeps the GPUs saturated with training first, mutually exclusive with infer_after
fields.inference: InferenceConfig sub-config used to run inference automatically after training when infer_after or infer_at_end is set
fields.trials_enabled: Enable the multi-trial GPU sweep (TrainScheduler) instead of a single training run
fields.trials_mode: Sweep dimension the trial scheduler varies: presence, physics, pair, log_energy, secondary, patch, input, context, reach, head, augmentation, clamp, stability, ema or amp
fields.presence_trials: Named trials each setting use_active_normalization and presence_balance (both keys required per trial); default is the 2x2 matrix none/A/B/AB, every trial repeated across the seeds list
fields.pair_trials: PairTrialsConfig sub-config for the loss-pair sweep pairing one fixed base component with each candidate second component and weight
fields.log_energy_trials: LogEnergyTrialsConfig sub-config for the log-energy weight sweep adding the term to the standard loss, one run per weight
fields.secondary_trials: SecondaryTrialsConfig sub-config for the secondary-channel selection sweep (strategy, count, sampling seed)
fields.patch_trials: PatchTrialsConfig sub-config for the rectangular patch-shape grid sweep under a constant pixel budget
fields.input_trials: Named input-channel presets (use_primary/use_secondaries/use_derived/use_aux) each scoped by a mandatory tracks key: all expands the secondary list to every channel of the dataset, reduced keeps the configured secondary selection; defaults cover the full grid of channel-amplitude-only, derived-phase-only and the combined stack on both scopes, every base variant duplicated as an explicit no-aux (-noaux) and with-aux (-aux) version
fields.context_trials: Rungs trained one run each, walking the spatial-context ladder at constant depth; every rung is a dict of label, backbone and model overrides (default a pixel_mlp rung of twenty 1x1 layers at width 1277 plus four local_cnn rungs of ten blocks, RF 1/9/29/41 via block_kernels mixes of 3x3 and 1x1, widths 1277/848/502/426, each within 0.5% of the default unet's parameters), and every backbone must exist in the registry
fields.reach_trials: ReachTrialsConfig sub-config for the size-matched architecture comparison at fixed reach, pairing a 33x33 local_cnn against a unet on a shared 32x32 patch at equal parameter count
fields.head_trials: HeadMatchingTrialsConfig sub-config for the head-and-matching grid crossing every selected head with every selected parameter-matching strategy on one fixed backbone
fields.augmentation_trials: AugmentationTrialsConfig sub-config for the cumulative augmentation ladder: no augmentation, then + horizontal flip, then + vertical flip, then + input noise at each configured strength
fields.clamp_trials: ClampTrialsConfig sub-config for the output-clamp ladder: no clamp, hard clamp, leaky clamp
fields.stability_trials: StabilityTrialsConfig sub-config for the training-stability arms: no lr warmup and no gradient clipping, then lr warmup alone per fraction, then gradient clipping alone per norm, then the first fraction paired with each norm
fields.ema_trials: EmaTrialsConfig sub-config for the weight-EMA arms: EMA off, then per configured decay one rung with the plain decay and one with the decay warmup ramp; the amp mode reuses the base config unchanged and needs no sub-config
fields.gpus: List of GPU device indices across which queued runs are distributed and launched in parallel; feeds the trials fan-out when trials are enabled and the per-seed fan-out of a plain multi-seed run otherwise
fields.gpus_file: Path of the live GPU pool control file for this fan-out; the scheduler seeds it from the gpus selection and re-reads it on every poll, so writing {"gpus": [...]} into it resizes the experiment while it runs (added devices pick up queued jobs, removed devices retire once the job in flight ends). Empty places gpu_pool.json inside the trials directory for trials, or the base run directory for a multi-seed fan-out
fields.poll_interval_s: Seconds between successive polls of the run queue while waiting for GPUs or completed jobs
fields.loss: LossConfig selecting the loss terms and their weights for the whole run, defaulting to parameter L1 with Hungarian matching, active normalization, presence balance and a cosine curve term

training/general/loss::LossConfig.summary: Enables and weights every term of the cube reconstruction training loss

fields.use_mse_curve: Enable mean-squared-error term comparing reconstructed and target reflectivity curves
fields.weight_mse_curve: Relative weight of the MSE curve term in the normalized weighted-average loss
fields.use_l1_curve: Enable L1 (mean absolute error) term on the reflectivity curve
fields.weight_l1_curve: Relative weight of the L1 curve term in the weighted-average loss
fields.use_huber_curve: Enable Huber term on the reflectivity curve, robust to profile outliers
fields.weight_huber_curve: Relative weight of the Huber curve term in the weighted-average loss
fields.huber_delta: Transition threshold between quadratic and linear regimes of the Huber curve loss
fields.use_charbonnier_curve: Enable Charbonnier (smooth robust-L1) term on the reflectivity curve
fields.weight_charbonnier_curve: Relative weight of the Charbonnier curve term in the weighted-average loss
fields.charbonnier_eps: Smoothing epsilon inside the Charbonnier square root near zero residual
fields.use_cosine_curve: Enable cosine-similarity term matching predicted and target curve shape along z
fields.weight_cosine_curve: Relative weight of the cosine-similarity curve term in the weighted-average loss
fields.use_log_energy_curve: Enable L1 term on the log ratio of predicted to target per-pixel curve energy, restoring the amplitude supervision the scale-invariant cosine term lacks; pixels with target norm below 1e-3 are excluded like in the cosine term
fields.weight_log_energy_curve: Relative weight of the log-energy curve term in the weighted-average loss
fields.use_param_l1: Enable L1 loss on matched, normalized Gaussian mixture parameters
fields.weight_param_l1: Relative weight of the parameter L1 term in the weighted-average loss
fields.use_param_huber: Enable Huber loss on matched, normalized Gaussian mixture parameters
fields.weight_param_huber: Relative weight of the parameter Huber term in the weighted-average loss
fields.param_huber_delta: Transition threshold between quadratic and linear regimes of the parameter Huber loss
fields.use_param_mse: Enable MSE loss on matched, normalized Gaussian mixture parameters
fields.weight_param_mse: Relative weight of the parameter MSE term in the weighted-average loss
fields.param_weights: Per-parameter weights for amplitude, mean, sigma; length must equal params_per_gaussian
fields.param_matching: Slot assignment before parameter losses: hungarian (permutes predictions to best GT match) or sorted_gt (positional, GT sorted only)
fields.use_active_normalization: Normalize parameter loss by summed slot weights instead of plain mean, avoiding dilution by empty slots
fields.presence_balance: Auto-balance active/inactive weights per Gaussian slot by inverse frequency of that slot's batch active fraction (clamped to [1e-3, 1-1e-3]), overriding active_weight and inactive_weight
fields.active_weight: Loss multiplier for slots with GT amplitude above the label run's activity threshold; ignored when presence_balance is on
fields.inactive_weight: Loss multiplier for slots with GT amplitude at or below the label run's activity threshold; ignored when presence_balance is on
fields.amp_focal_gamma: Focal exponent upweighting hard amplitude errors; 0 disables focal weighting entirely
fields.amp_focal_delta: Denominator offset controlling how fast the amplitude focal weighting saturates; only active when amp_focal_gamma>0
fields.use_smoothness_tv: Enable total-variation penalty on normalized parameter maps across spatial neighbors
fields.weight_smoothness_tv: Relative weight of the spatial total-variation smoothness term in the weighted-average loss
fields.use_total_power: Enable relative-error term matching integrated total power of predicted vs target curves
fields.weight_total_power: Relative weight of the total-power term in the weighted-average loss
fields.use_moments: Enable term matching mass, mean, and spread moments of the curves
fields.weight_moments: Relative weight of the moments term in the weighted-average loss
fields.moments_weights: Per-moment sub-weights for mass, mean, and spread combined in the moments loss
fields.power_floor: Integrated target power a pixel must exceed to enter the total-power and moments terms; pixels at or below it are masked out, the share kept is logged as loss_monitor/moment_valid_frac, and a batch with none contributes 0.0 and is flagged in loss_monitor/moment_empty_batch; also floors those terms' power-normalization denominators

training/general/optimization::Optimizer.summary: AdamW betas/eps defaults and lr-scale factor consumed by the trainer; weight_decay is an inert default always overridden per param group by architecture configs

fields.betas: AdamW (beta1, beta2) exponential moving-average decay rates for the gradient and squared-gradient moments, set as the default for every param group via setdefault
fields.type: optimizer family: adamw, adam, sgd or rmsprop; the adaptive families read betas and eps, sgd and rmsprop read momentum and nesterov
fields.momentum: momentum factor of the sgd and rmsprop families; ignored by adamw and adam
fields.nesterov: whether sgd uses Nesterov momentum; requires a positive momentum and is ignored by the other families
fields.eps: AdamW epsilon added to the square root of the second-moment estimate in the update denominator for numerical stability
fields.weight_decay: AdamW decoupled weight-decay default; only applied via setdefault when a param group omits weight_decay, which none of the current architecture configs do
fields.lr_scale: multiplier applied in place to every param group's lr; set by ConfigFactory to batch_size / lr_reference_batch_size when scale_lr_with_batch is enabled, else 1.0

training/general/optimization::Scheduler.summary: per-epoch multiplicative schedule scaling each param group's own base lr across training

fields.type: schedule shape: cosine_annealing, constant, linear, polynomial, exponential, or step
fields.epochs: epoch horizon (T_max) the cosine_annealing, linear, polynomial, and exponential schedules ramp down over
fields.eta_min: floor learning rate every schedule type except constant decays toward, given as an absolute rate but converted internally to a ratio against the first param group's base lr
fields.step_size: epoch interval between multiplicative decays, used only when type is step
fields.gamma: multiplicative decay factor applied every step_size epochs, used only when type is step
fields.power: exponent controlling the decay curvature of the polynomial schedule, used only when type is polynomial

training/general/optimization::WarmupCon.summary: initial learning-rate ramp multiplied on top of the scheduler's factor until warmup completes

fields.warmup_fraction: fraction of the run's total optimizer steps over which the learning rate ramps from warmup_start_factor to full rate, resolved into a step count at train start; 0 or warmup_enabled=False skips warmup
fields.warmup_start_factor: starting learning rate at step 0 as a fraction of the base rate, e.g. 0.1 starts at 10 percent
fields.warmup_enabled: master toggle for the warmup ramp; when False the base/scheduled rate applies from step 0
fields.warmup_mode: ramp shape from warmup_start_factor to 1.0: linear, cosine, exponential, or polynomial
fields.warmup_poly_power: exponent controlling the ramp curvature, used only when warmup_mode is polynomial

training/general/optimization::EarlyStop.summary: early-stopping policy halting training when validation loss stops improving

fields.patience: consecutive validation checks without a loss improvement of at least min_delta tolerated before stopping
fields.min_delta: minimum validation-loss improvement required to reset the patience counter
fields.restore_best: whether to reload the best-checkpoint weights once training ends, whether by early stopping or reaching max epochs

training/general/optimization::GradientC.summary: gradient-clipping strategy bounding the global gradient norm each training step

fields.clip_mode: clipping strategy: disabled, fixed, adaptive_percentile, or adaptive_mean_std
fields.max_grad_norm: fixed global-norm threshold gradients are rescaled down to when exceeded, used only when clip_mode is fixed
fields.adaptive_window: number of recent global-norm samples kept to compute the adaptive threshold, used only when clip_mode is adaptive_percentile or adaptive_mean_std
fields.adaptive_percentile: percentile (0-100) of the recent-norm window used as the clip threshold, used only when clip_mode is adaptive_percentile
fields.adaptive_mean_std_k: number of standard deviations above the recent-norm window mean used as the clip threshold, used only when clip_mode is adaptive_mean_std
fields.clip_epsilon: small constant added to the gradient norm denominator to avoid division by zero when scaling
fields.log_histogram_freq: step interval between gradient-norm histogram logs to TensorBoard

training/general/run::TrainingPathsConfi.summary: Filesystem locations for a training run's dataset, ground-truth parameters, and secondary channels

fields.dataset_path: root directory of the preprocessed channel-stack dataset (dataset.json, layout, geometry field)
fields.parameters_path: path to the .npy Gaussian ground-truth parameters produced by parameter extraction
fields.secondary_labels: tuple of secondary-channel labels (e.g. CH01) selecting which channels join the primary channel; empty/None uses all channels
fields.fingerprint_dataset: whether the run hashes every dataset artifact (sha256) into meta/dataset_fingerprint.json, so the exact data behind a result stays provable after the generator is re-run; costs one linear read of the dataset at run start

training/general/run::RunPathsConfig.summary: TrainingPathsConfig extended with the batch-run root used by benchmark, cross-validation, and tuning entries

fields.log_base_dir: base directory under which each queued run's tagged output subdirectory and TensorBoard logs are written

training/general/run::TrainingQueueConfi.summary: Full training-loop, optimization, scheduling, gradient-clipping, and data-split hyperparameters for one queued run

fields.epochs: total number of training epochs to run
fields.scheduler_epochs: epoch horizon over which the LR scheduler decays; None falls back to epochs
fields.validation_frequency: run validation every N epochs, always including the final epoch
fields.batch_size: number of patch samples per optimization step in the dataloader
fields.num_workers: number of dataloader worker processes used for parallel patch assembly
fields.prefetch_factor: number of batches each dataloader worker prefetches ahead
fields.eta_min: minimum learning-rate floor the scheduler decays toward
fields.early_stop_patience: epochs without validation improvement before training stops early
fields.early_stop_min_delta: minimum validation-loss improvement required to reset early-stopping patience
fields.log_all_losses: log every individual loss component term to TensorBoard, not just the total
fields.log_debug: enable the tracker's debug mode, adding gradient NaN/Inf checks and extra diagnostic logging
fields.use_amp: autocast the forward/loss pass to bfloat16; raises at startup if the GPU lacks bf16 support
fields.compile_model: compile the model forward with torch.compile before training; the first step pays a compilation delay, later steps run the optimized kernels, and saved checkpoints stay byte-identical to an uncompiled run
fields.compile_mode: torch.compile mode: default balances compile time and speed, reduce-overhead targets small batches via CUDA graphs, max-autotune searches the widest kernel space
fields.channels_last: keep the model weights and every 4-D batch in channels_last (NHWC) memory layout, which speeds up convolutions under AMP on tensor-core GPUs
fields.activation_checkpointing: fnmatch patterns of dotted submodule names to wrap in gradient checkpointing (e.g. encoder*); wrapped activations are recomputed in backward, trading compute for activation memory; empty disables it, a pattern matching nothing fails loudly
fields.gradient_accumulation_steps: minibatches accumulated before each optimizer step, scaling the effective batch size
fields.abort_on_nonfinite_loss: raise and stop training on a NaN/Inf loss instead of skipping the batch with a warning
fields.use_ema: maintain an exponential moving average of model weights, used for evaluation and checkpointing
fields.use_swa: maintain an equal-weight stochastic average of the model weights from the SWA start epoch on; at the end of training the averaged model gets its batch-norm statistics refreshed, is scored on validation and saved as swa_model.pt
fields.swa_start_fraction: fraction of the epoch budget after which each finished epoch joins the stochastic weight average (0.75 averages the last quarter of training)
fields.optimizer_type: optimizer family training runs on: adamw (decoupled weight decay), adam, sgd (momentum, optional Nesterov) or rmsprop
fields.momentum: momentum factor of the sgd and rmsprop families; ignored by adamw and adam
fields.nesterov: whether sgd uses Nesterov momentum; requires a positive momentum and is ignored by the other families
fields.ema_decay: target decay rate of the weight EMA; closer to 1 averages over more steps
fields.ema_warmup: ramp the effective EMA decay as min(decay, (1+t)/(10+t)) over the update count t so early updates track the model closely before settling at the target decay
fields.resume: resume training from the last checkpoint in the run directory
fields.reserve_vram: fill spare GPU memory into this process's allocator cache before the first batch so concurrent jobs cannot claim the device
fields.vram_keep_free_gb: gigabytes of GPU memory the reservation leaves unclaimed on the device
fields.scale_lr_with_batch: scale the optimizer lr_scale linearly by batch_size / lr_reference_batch_size, else keep lr_scale at 1.0
fields.lr_reference_batch_size: baseline batch size the learning-rate scaling ratio is computed against
fields.lr_multiplier: factor applied to every param-group learning rate on top of the batch-size rule
fields.scheduler_type: learning-rate schedule: cosine_annealing, constant, linear, polynomial, exponential, or step
fields.scheduler_step_size: epoch interval between decays for the step scheduler
fields.scheduler_gamma: multiplicative decay factor applied at each step-scheduler drop
fields.warmup_enabled: ramp the learning rate up from a fraction of its target value at the start of training
fields.warmup_fraction: fraction of the run's total optimizer steps over which the warmup ramp runs, resolved into a step count at train start
fields.warmup_mode: warmup ramp shape: linear, cosine, exponential, or polynomial
fields.warmup_poly_power: exponent used when warmup_mode is polynomial
fields.clip_mode: gradient-clipping strategy: disabled, fixed, adaptive_percentile, or adaptive_mean_std
fields.max_grad_norm: fixed gradient-norm threshold used when clip_mode is fixed
fields.clip_adaptive_window: number of recent step norms kept to compute the adaptive clip threshold
fields.clip_adaptive_percentile: percentile of the recent-norm window used as the clip bound when clip_mode is adaptive_percentile
fields.clip_adaptive_mean_std_k: std-dev multiplier k in mean + k*std used as the clip bound when clip_mode is adaptive_mean_std
fields.patch_size: z and width in pixels of training patches cropped from the input stack, (H, W) may be rectangular for fully-convolutional backbones
fields.patch_stride: per-axis (vertical, horizontal) pixel stride between overlapping extracted patches
fields.use_symmetric_padding: pad scene borders with symmetric (mirror) padding instead of zero (constant) padding so edge patches stay fully covered
fields.train_rows: row line range (start, end) assigned to the training split, paired with the dataset's full range extent
fields.val_rows: row line range (start, end) assigned to the validation split, paired with the dataset's full range extent
fields.test_rows: row line range (start, end) assigned to the test split, paired with the dataset's full range extent
fields.snapshot_every_n_epochs: Save a weights-only epoch snapshot to checkpoints/epoch_<N>.pt every N epochs (EMA weights when EMA is on); 0 disables. Snapshots feed the training-evolution animation and cost one state_dict write each

training/general/runtime::TrainingLoopCo.summary: Core optimization-loop cadence, precision, EMA, and failure-handling knobs consumed by the Trainer

fields.use_amp: Enable autocast mixed precision to bfloat16 during train/eval forward passes; raises at construction if the GPU lacks bf16 support
fields.compile_model: compile the model forward with torch.compile before training; the first step pays a compilation delay, later steps run the optimized kernels, and saved checkpoints stay byte-identical to an uncompiled run
fields.compile_mode: torch.compile mode: default balances compile time and speed, reduce-overhead targets small batches via CUDA graphs, max-autotune searches the widest kernel space
fields.channels_last: keep the model weights and every 4-D batch in channels_last (NHWC) memory layout, which speeds up convolutions under AMP on tensor-core GPUs

fields.use_ema: Maintain a WeightEma shadow copy of model weights, decayed by ema_decay, for evaluation/checkpointing
fields.use_swa: maintain an equal-weight stochastic average of the model weights from the SWA start epoch on; at the end of training the averaged model gets its batch-norm statistics refreshed, is scored on validation and saved as swa_model.pt

fields.snapshot_every_n_epochs: Save a weights-only epoch snapshot to checkpoints/epoch_<N>.pt every N epochs (EMA weights when EMA is on); 0 disables. Snapshots feed the training-evolution animation and cost one state_dict write each

training/general/runtime::MemoryConfig.summary: Pre-training VRAM reservation to protect other GPU users

fields.reserve_vram: Before training starts, greedily allocate spare GPU memory down to vram_keep_free_gb via VramReservation to block other users from claiming it
fields.vram_keep_free_gb: Gigabytes of free VRAM left unclaimed on the device when reserve_vram is enabled

resources::ResourceConfig.summary: Background system-resource monitor polling RAM/VRAM/swap/shared-memory and raising threshold warnings

fields.enabled: Master toggle running the background ResourceMonitor thread during training
fields.log_to_tensorboard: Record every sampled resource metric (RAM, VRAM, swap, shm, CPU, disk I/O, process stats, per-GPU utilization/temp/power) as flat TensorBoard scalars under system/resources
fields.warn_ram_pct: System RAM usage percentage that triggers a warning log

inference/backbone::BackboneInferenceEnt.summary: Entry config for the scheduler that runs sliding-window backbone inference over multiple runs, queuing one worker process per run across a fixed pool of GPUs

fields.runs_dir: Any path holding runs: one run directory, a seed sweep, a trial sweep, an experiment workspace or a whole runs tree; every run at any depth below it (a directory holding meta/model_config.json) is discovered. A missing directory is an error
fields.run_filter: Names selecting runs under runs_dir: a run's path relative to runs_dir, a directory below runs_dir whose runs are all taken, or a run's own directory name; empty selects every run found. An entry naming no run raises FileNotFoundError listing the runs found
fields.gpus: GPU device indices the GpuQueue cycles jobs across, default [0]; one run is launched per free GPU concurrently until the queue drains
fields.gpus_file: Path of the live GPU pool control file for this inference queue; the scheduler seeds it from the gpus selection and re-reads it on every poll, so writing {"gpus": [...]} into it resizes the queue while it runs (added devices pick up queued runs, removed devices retire once the run in flight ends). Empty places gpu_pool.json inside the batch's work directory under logs/inference
fields.poll_interval_s: seconds GpuQueue sleeps between reap/launch cycles while jobs are running or queued, default 5.0
fields.inference: InferenceConfig used for every worker run, with run_directory replaced per-run, save_cubes=True, cpu_workers=16 and gif_axes=['z','col','row']; all other InferenceConfig fields (split, checkpoint_name, save_plots, etc.) keep their normal defaults
fields.skip_completed: Whether runs already holding a completed inference stamp for inference.split are left alone, so relaunching over an experiment scores only the runs still missing it; off re-scores every selected run into a fresh timestamped stamp

inference/general::InferencePaths.summary: Names of output subdirectories and result filenames written under an inference run's output directory

fields.figures_subdir: Subdirectory name under the inference output directory for static figure PNGs

fields.logs_subdir: Subdirectory name under the inference output directory for the run log file

inference/general::TargetDatasetConfig.summary: Scores a trained run on a dataset it was never trained on: the checkpoint, patch geometry, input channels and training normalization statistics stay, the scene, its labels, the secondary channels and the scored crop change

fields.enabled: Score the run on the target dataset below instead of its own split; the split must stay 'test' and region_override unset

inference/general::InferenceConfig.summary: Drives a full backbone cube inference run: loading, prediction, physics evaluation, plotting, and reporting

tuning/general::TuningConfig.summary: Optuna hyperparameter search controls: trial budget, seeding, pruning, and artifact emission

fields.n_trials: target number of completed trials per model's Optuna study, resumable across runs (existing completed/pruned trials count toward it)
fields.n_epochs: training epochs evaluated per trial before scoring it, applied to both the training loop and its LR scheduler
fields.base_seed: base RNG seed: offset by the worker index seeds the Optuna TPE sampler, offset by trial number seeds each trial's weight init and augmentation
fields.early_stop_patience: epochs without validation improvement before a trial's training is halted early
fields.pruner_n_startup_trials: startup-trial count shared by optuna.pruners.MedianPruner (trials exempt from pruning) and the TPESampler (trials of random search before it switches to TPE)
fields.pruner_n_warmup_steps: epochs within a trial before MedianPruner is allowed to prune that trial
fields.search_lr: Whether the study samples the model configuration's learning rates, weight decays and dropout (its tunable_lr_params). Defines the study, so it cannot change on resume
fields.search_arch: Whether the study samples the model configuration's architecture fields (its tunable_arch_params: feature widths, bottleneck factor, activation, normalization, upsampling and the like). Defines the study, so it cannot change on resume
fields.search_batch: Whether the study samples the training batch size from batch_sizes. The trial puts the drawn size on the loader and rescales the optimizer by batch over lr_reference_batch_size as every training entry does, so a tuned rate stays quoted at the reference batch and a downstream run with the same batch reproduces it. The best size is recorded on a training.batch_size decision axis of a sequence block. Defines the study, so it cannot change on resume
fields.batch_sizes: Batch sizes the study may pick when search_batch is on; every size must fit the GPU with the largest architecture the study may draw. Defines the study, so it cannot change on resume
fields.plateau_patience: Finished trials (completed or pruned) without the best value improving before the study stops; 0 runs the trial target out. The finished trials are walked in trial order, a completed trial beating the best by at least plateau_min_delta resets the count, and every worker reads the same verdict off the shared study. Changeable on resume
fields.plateau_min_delta: Smallest improvement of the best value, relative to its value at the last counted improvement, that resets the plateau count; 0 counts any improvement, which lets seed noise keep a converged study alive. Changeable on resume
fields.time_budget_h: Hours after which a worker starts no further trial; the trial in flight still finishes, so a launch with a hard time limit must allow the budget plus one trial. 0 sets no budget. Changeable on resume
fields.emit_trial_docs: whether to write per-trial training-documentation artifacts to the run directory
fields.emit_study_plots: whether to render Optuna study-level visualization plots after each model's sweep completes
fields.keep_trial_checkpoints: Whether the checkpoint files (best_model.pt, last.pt, final_model.pt, epoch snapshots) of a finished trial stay in its run directory. Off by default: nothing loads them again, the trial's parameters live in the study, and a study of hundreds of trials would otherwise hold hundreds of gigabytes of weights that a sequence workspace pull copies back

fields.gpus_file: Path of the live GPU pool control file for this queue; the scheduler seeds it from the gpus selection and re-reads it on every poll, so writing {"gpus": [...]} into it resizes the run while it is in flight (added devices pick up queued jobs, removed devices retire once the job in flight ends). Empty places gpu_pool.json inside the run directory
fields.heads: Output heads crossed with every tuned backbone; each backbone x head pair gets its own study (default [conv])

diagnostics::WeightXrayThresholds.summary: Numeric thresholds classifying weight-tensor pathologies during the weight-xray checkpoint diagnostic

fields.dead_abs_threshold: absolute magnitude below which any analyzed tensor's element counts as dead, feeds the per-tensor frac_dead statistic
fields.dead_fraction_warn: frac_dead level at or above which a tensor is flagged high_sparsity (warning), 0.50 default
fields.dead_fraction_critical: frac_dead level at or above which a tensor is flagged dead_tensor (critical), 0.95 default
fields.dead_unit_norm_frac: fraction of a weight matrix's max row/column norm at or below which that output or input unit counts as dead
fields.dead_unit_fraction_warn: fraction of dead output units (dead_output_frac) at or above which dead_neurons is a warning instead of info
fields.uniform_cv_threshold: coefficient-of-variation (std/mean_abs) at or below which weight or norm_scale tensors of 8+ elements flag as near-uniform
fields.constant_std_threshold: tensor standard deviation at or below which it is flagged critical as constant
fields.rank_ratio_warn: effective-to-full rank ratio at or below which a weight matrix flags rank_deficient (warning), 0.50 default
fields.rank_ratio_critical: effective-to-full rank ratio at or below which a weight matrix flags rank_collapse (critical), 0.10 default
fields.explode_abs_threshold: max absolute value in any analyzed tensor at or above which it flags large_magnitude (warning)
fields.spectral_norm_warn: top singular value of a weight matrix at or above which it flags large_spectral_norm (warning)
fields.bias_abs_threshold: max absolute bias value at or above which a bias tensor flags large_bias (warning)
fields.norm_scale_dead_value: absolute value below which a normalization-layer scale (gamma) element counts as collapsed
fields.norm_scale_dead_frac: fraction of norm-scale elements below norm_scale_dead_value at or above which scale_collapse warns
fields.running_var_dead_value: BatchNorm running_var value below which a channel counts as dead
fields.running_var_dead_frac: fraction of running_var elements below running_var_dead_value at or above which dead_channel_var warns
fields.init_ratio_low: lower bound on std*sqrt(fan_in) below which a weight raises an info scale_low observation
fields.init_ratio_high: upper bound on std*sqrt(fan_in) above which a weight raises an info scale_high observation
fields.duplicate_cosine: absolute cosine similarity between two normalized output-unit rows at or above which they count as a duplicate pair
fields.duplicate_fraction_warn: ratio of duplicate-pair count to output-unit count at or above which duplicate_units is a warning instead of info
